prompt: The client asks: "How should we respond to a new low-cost rival?" Fact sheet: the rival prices 30% below us; it targets small customers, who are 20% of our revenue and 5% of our profit; our large customers rate our service 9 out of 10; the rival has no service team; we have 200 sales staff. Which is the best recommendation?

options.text: The rival targets small customers, who are 20% of revenue but only 5% of profit, and our large customers rate our service 9 out of 10, which the rival can't match. The main risk is that the rival moves up to larger customers. Putting it together, don't cut prices across the board; protect the large customers.
options.feedback: The answer comes last. Lead with the recommendation, then support it.

options.text: Don't cut prices across the board; protect the large customers. The rival targets small customers, who are 20% of revenue but only 5% of profit, and our large customers rate our service 9 out of 10, which the rival can't match. The main risk is that the rival moves up to larger customers, so the next step is to monitor churn among large accounts and prepare a lower-cost offer if it rises.
options.feedback: Right. It leads with the answer, backs it with the numbers that matter, and gives a risk and a next step.
